question: On http://localhost:8092/ there's a paragraph that reads "This is a paragraph of text. It demonstrates the paragraph element in HTML." My step `{"find": {"selector": "p", "elementText": "demonstrates the paragraph element"}}` times out even though that text is right there on the page. What's wrong?

facts.text: `elementText` matches the element's entire visible text (with whitespace normalized), not a substring, so a fragment of the paragraph doesn't match.
To match part of the text, wrap the value in slashes as a regular expression, such as `"/demonstrates the paragraph element/"`, or give the paragraph's full text.

must_not: `elementText` matches any element whose text contains the value.
`selector` and `elementText` can't be combined, so one of them is ignored or makes the step fail.

run.does: that finds the paragraph by part of its text

wrong.why: blames the selector and calls elementText a substring match
wrong.answer:
`elementText` already matches any element whose text contains your value, so the fragment is fine. The `selector` is the problem: when both are set, Doc Detective uses only the selector. Drop it:

```json
{ "find": { "elementText": "/demonstrates the paragraph element/" } }
```
